title: Your first web page
lesson:
A web page is a text file written in **HTML**, which marks up what each part *is*: this is a heading, this is a paragraph, this is a list. The browser decides how it looks (CSS changes that later). ``` Shamba Notes

Shamba Notes

What we planted this season.

``` - Things in angle brackets are **tags**. Most come in pairs: `

` opens a paragraph and `

` closes it. What's between is the **content**. - `` on the first line tells the browser to use modern rules. - `` holds information *about* the page: the `` shown on the tab, the character set (`utf-8`, so Swahili, accents and emoji all work) and the viewport line that makes it fit phones. - `<body>` holds what you see. Headings go from `<h1>` (one per page, the main title) down to `<h6>`. - Tags **nest** like boxes: close the inner one before the outer one. `<p><b>yes</b></p>` is right; `<p><b>yes</p></b>` is broken. Open the file in a browser to see it (or press **preview**). Archie's page checker catches tags left open or closed in the wrong order on every save.

example.code:
Shamba Notes

What we planted this season, and how it grew.

Maize

Planted in March, harvested in July.
notes: One h1, then h2 for sections.
b and i inside a paragraph: nested correctly.

exercises.title: A page about you
exercises.prompt: Make a page with the title "About me", an h1 with your name, a paragraph about yourself, and an h2 "Things I want to build" with a paragraph under it.
exercises.starter:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title></title>
</head>
<body>

</body>
</html>
hints: The title goes in the head; everything you see goes in the body.
exercises.solution:
Sam

I build things and I'm learning to code.

Things I want to build

A water tank alarm and a game.

exercises.prompt: This page has tags closed in the wrong order and tags never closed. Use the checker's messages (on the right after you save) to fix it until there are no errors. Keep all the text.

choices: Information about the page: title, charset, viewport

quiz.q: How many h1 should a page usually have?
quiz.why: One main heading; sections use h2, h3…

cards.a: What each part of the page is (heading, paragraph, list…), not how it looks.
So the page fits phone screens instead of showing a tiny desktop page.

explain: Explain your first web page to someone who has never programmed, in your own words, with an example you make up.
